findings.title: §4.6's pre-existing "taken over ... silently" claim now overlaps confusingly with the newly-written lock_taken paragraph
findings.detail: Line 311 (untouched by this diff) says a generated holder "is taken over on the next call by anyone, silently." Five lines later, the diff's new paragraph (lines 316-320) draws a much narrower silence: only a generated *acquirer* taking over a generated holder, unforced, "records nothing" — a named acquirer's takeover of the same generated holder does append a lock_taken event (cmd_next.go's `case orphaned:` when `!r.genID`, internal/cli/cmd_next.go:206-209). Reusing the word "silently" for the (unrelated, still-true) absence of the `ask: owner` prompt right next to a paragraph that uses "quietly"/"records nothing" for the absence of an audit event invites a reader to conflate the two. Task 3's brief only asked for the one sentence at ~line 315 to be rewritten, but the result now reads as self-contradictory within the same subsection unless line 311 is also qualified.

findings.title: Task 8's loss-simulation test helpers are duplicated with divergent names across the two record test files
findings.detail: cmd_record_test.go (package cli) defines readOnlyEventLog (:338), directoryEventLog (:357) and assertStreakLoss (:370); record_reviewer_test.go (package cli_test) defines breakEventAppend (internal/cli/record_reviewer_test.go:549), breakEventRead (internal/cli/record_reviewer_test.go:567) and assertStreakWarning (internal/cli/record_reviewer_test.go:596). Each pair is byte-for-byte the same body (chmod 0400 + skip-if-writable; replace the event log with a directory; assert exit 0 plus one warning sentence) implementing the same #16 concept, just under different names because the two files sit in different packages. The functions can't be merged given the package split, but nothing stops them from sharing a name — as written, a reader scanning both files for "the read-loss helper" has to know two different identifiers for the same idea.

findings.title: warnStreakLoss inlines its warning string instead of following the local excludeWarning(err) helper convention
findings.detail: cmd_init.go's excludeWarning(err) (internal/cli/cmd_init.go:425-427) is a small named function returning "info/exclude not written: " + err.Error(), used by both cmd_init.go and cmd_next.go for the same warnings-contract pattern this task extends. warnStreakLoss instead builds "attempt-streak reset not recorded: "+err.Error() inline inside the append call. Not wrong, but it departs from the one-sentence-per-named-function shape the warnings contract otherwise uses for its two other producers.
